open_obligations: Confirm that the forthcoming protocol in Buhl et al. is prover-estimator debate (the setting names it as the example protocol).
Check whether Buhl et al. need stability for safety or only for usefulness, given Brown-Cohen et al.'s distinction.
Check that Buhl et al.'s informal stability statement matches Definition 5.3.
in.other_title: No-obfuscated-arguments assumption and the stability requirement it brings
in.rationale: Buhl et al. require a debate protocol that avoids obfuscated arguments and rely on a forthcoming protocol that needs a stability assumption: the computation is not sensitive to small variations in input probabilities. Brown-Cohen et al. formalise rho-stability (argument validity cannot hinge on arbitrarily small changes in subclaim probabilities) for prover-estimator debate and require it only for usefulness, not safety.
in.scope: proposed DEPENDS_ON: the debate safety case's requirement of a protocol free of obfuscated arguments, which relies on a stability assumption

open_obligations: Note that loss of completeness without stability may still make debate useless on some questions.
Check whether cross-examination-style consistency checks were added, which Buhl et al. suggest.
Check that the safety claim holds with approximate rather than exact equilibria.
out.other_title: Open: relax the stability assumption and avoid gerrymandering across subclaims
out.rationale: Buhl et al. ask for protocols that do not require stability, since it may not hold for relevant queries. Brown-Cohen et al. state rho-stability is required only for usefulness (completeness), not for safety: without it an honest estimator can still beat any incorrect argument by a dishonest prover; it does not address the gerrymandering concern across subclaims.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether the stability assumption of prover-estimator debate is needed for safety, for recursive debate

text: The authors state that prover-estimator debate makes Alice's task harder because Bob can defeat an argument by assigning low probabilities to many subclaims, which rules out delicate but correct arguments that are highly sensitive to subclaim probabilities. They formalise a rho-stability requirement that argument validity cannot hinge on arbitrarily small changes in subclaim probabilities, and require it only for usefulness, not safety: without stability an honest estimator can still win against any incorrect argument by a dishonest prover.
title: rho-stability assumption: needed for usefulness, not for safety
